name: Test insurance blood and urine profiles
sector: health care: medical laboratory testing and health services
summary: Life insurers ask applicants for blood and urine so their underwriters can check lipids, glucose, liver and kidney function, PSA, HIV and hepatitis antibodies, nicotine and drugs. Kits collected at paramedical exams arrive by overnight courier; lab assistants check the signed consent, seals and insurer lab code, match the kit to its order, centrifuge and aliquot, and the profile runs on the shared core laboratory analysers. Technologists review held results, rerun and confirm reactive screens, and release the profile, which goes electronically to the insurer within about 48 hours of arrival. Kits with missing signatures, no matching order, no urine or spoiled serum cause holds, chases to examiners and recollections.

baseline.org_archetype: The insurance laboratory testing line of a large Canadian laboratory company, testing about 15,000 insurance kits a month in the core laboratory of its Brampton site.
baseline.notes: Paper laboratory authorization slips with ePara electronic files; LIS linked to the insurance order management system; ACORD and custom electronic delivery to insurers.

trigger: A blood and urine (or urine-only) kit from a paramedical exam arrives at the laboratory by overnight courier.
end_state: The insurer's profile is released and transmitted to the insurer and the case file, or the kit is reported not testable and a recollection requested.

volume.seasonality: Follows insurance applications: lower in summer and late December, higher in spring and autumn.

evidence.note: Matches the organisation file's estimate (about 15,000 kits from about 16,000 paramedical exams a month; some exams are vitals-only). A comparable US insurance laboratory drew about 65 percent of its specimens from its own paramedical exams (hh2012).

Assistants receive and open kits, check the laboratory authorization form and seals, centrifuge, aliquot and load analysers. FTE 11 of the 20 left after core testing claims 40. Wage Job Bank 33101 times 1.35; Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Medical laboratory technologist, chemistry and haematology

evidence.note: Technologists review held results, rerun and confirm reactive screens and release profiles in the shared core laboratory. FTE 5 of about 42 left. Wage Job Bank 32120; Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Medical evidence quality reviewer
roles.department: Insurance order desk and case management

evidence.note: Insurance evidence reviewers resolve kits that do not match an order, chase missing consent or lab codes with examiners and tell case management when a recollection is needed; 1.5 of 15. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Laboratory medical director or clinical scientist (clinical pathologist, biochemist, microbiologist)
roles.department: Community laboratory testing (The model laboratory Laboratories)

evidence.note: A laboratory medical director or clinical scientist reviews confirmed positive HIV and hepatitis results before release; small share. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

systems.name: Laboratory information system (orders, accessioning, results, autoverification rules)
Instrument middleware with autoverification and rerun rules
Automated chemistry and immunoassay analysers on track lines
Insurance Order Management System with Paraweb ordering and iCARE status hub
ePara electronic medical evidence collection on examiner laptops
Electronic results delivery to insurers (ACORD and custom formats)
Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording
Quality management system software (document control, CAPA, training records)

steps.name: Receive the overnight courier packs
steps.description: In the morning a lab assistant signs for the bags of courier packs, scans each waybill, checks that packs are cool and not crushed or leaking, and moves them to the insurance bench in the refrigerator.

evidence.note: Kits shipped by Purolator to the Brampton laboratory, refrigerated until pick-up (dyn_kit2020, dyn_faq). Times are estimates; most packs arrive in one morning delivery.

steps.name: Open the kit and check the authorization form and seals
steps.description: The assistant opens the clamshell and checks the laboratory authorization form: the applicant's signature on the notice, consent and chain of custody section, the examiner's signature, the insurer's lab code, the recorded urine temperature, the signed tamper-evident tape intact, and barcode labels on every tube matching the form.

error.defect_description: A missing signature or broken seal is not noticed.

control.basis: PIPEDA consent principle: express consent of the applicant before testing and disclosure of sensitive health information, evidenced by the signed notice and consent on the laboratory slip

next.condition: missing signature, lab code or label, or broken seal

evidence.note: Required signatures, seal, lab code and urine temperature (dyn_kit2020, crl_instr); express consent for sensitive information (opc_consent). The 7 percent deficiency rate is an estimate; electronic slips reduce but do not remove incomplete entries (examone2016 describes the problem).

steps.name: Accession the kit against the insurance order
steps.description: The assistant scans the kit barcode; the LIS looks up the order sent from the order management system and the examiner's ePara upload to get the applicant's identity, the insurer and the insurer's test profile, and registers the specimens under that order.

error.defect_description: Kit registered against the wrong order.

control.basis: ISO 15189 and CAP requirements for unique specimen identification and traceability

evidence.note: Insurer-specific and custom profiles (dyn_car); profile contents (hh2012). The 8 percent unmatched share (kits arriving before the ePara file or with mistyped details) is an estimate.

steps.name: Hold the kit and log the deficiency
steps.description: The assistant keeps the specimens refrigerated on the hold shelf, records the deficiency in the LIS against the kit barcode and opens a nonconformance for the examiner, so the evidence reviewer can chase it.

evidence.note: Specimen acceptability protocols in the quality system (dyn_licences). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Ask the examiner or case management for the missing item
steps.description: The evidence reviewer phones or messages the examiner for a missing signature page or lab code, or asks case management to confirm the insurer's lab code and profile; a missing applicant signature needs a signed consent obtained from the applicant.

evidence.note: Specimens are not tested without the applicant's signed authorization (crl_instr). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the correction from the examiner or applicant
steps.description: The examiner faxes or uploads the signed form or confirms the lab code; for a missing applicant signature the examiner must revisit or the insurer decides whether to reorder.

evidence.note: Non-viable specimens may need recollection, decided by the carrier (dyn_faq). Waits and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Resolve a kit that does not match an order
steps.description: The evidence reviewer searches the order management system by applicant name, date of birth, examiner and insurer, links the kit to the right order or creates the lab order with the insurer's standard profile, and confirms with case management when the order details conflict.

error.defect_description: Kit linked to the wrong applicant.

evidence.note: Common practice when kits arrive before or without matching electronic order data; estimate.

steps.name: Centrifuge and aliquot, and check specimen quality
steps.description: The assistant centrifuges any unspun serum tube, checks that serum was separated and poured off, looks for haemolysis, lipaemia and low volume, checks the urine preservative tube volume, and pours aliquots for chemistry, immunoassay and urine testing.

error.defect_description: Haemolysed or short specimen tested without a flag.

control.basis: Documented specimen acceptance criteria (ISO 15189; laboratory specimen acceptability protocol)

next.condition: part of the profile cannot be tested
not testable: no urine, quantity not sufficient, haemolysed or too old

evidence.note: SST should be centrifuged within 2 to 4 hours and serum poured off (dyn_kit2020); delayed centrifugation causes errors (examone2016); a urine sample must accompany every blood kit (crl_instr). Shares are estimates.

steps.name: Load blood and urine aliquots on the analysers
steps.description: The assistant places the aliquots on the track or analyser racks in the shared core laboratory; the analysers download the insurer's profile from the LIS.

evidence.note: Insurance profiles run on chemistry and immunoassay analysers (hh2012 lists the analytes). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Test what the specimen allows and note the missing tests
steps.description: When only part of the profile can be done (for example no urine, or too little serum for every assay), the assistant prioritises the tests the insurer marks as required, records the tests not done with a reason, and the evidence reviewer is alerted.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Run the insurer's profile on the analysers
steps.description: The analysers run lipids, glucose and HbA1c, liver and kidney tests, PSA for older men, HIV and hepatitis antibody screens, cotinine and drug screens and urinalysis as the profile requires; no one works on the specimens during the run.

evidence.note: Profile contents (hh2012); PSA in the male blood profile (equitable1343); urine HIV and nicotine tests (empire_fug). Run time is an estimate.

steps.name: Apply autoverification rules
steps.description: Middleware compares each result with the insurer's reporting rules, instrument flags and QC status, releases clean results to the final review queue and holds reactive screens, out-of-range values, instrument flags and specimen-quality comments for a technologist.

error.defect_description: A rule releases a result that needed review.

control.basis: Validated autoverification rules under ISO 15189 and CAP

evidence.note: Autoverification is described for the core laboratory in the organisation file; the 25 percent hold share for multi-analyte insurance profiles is an estimate.

steps.name: Technologist reviews held results
steps.description: A medical laboratory technologist looks at each held result with its flags, QC and specimen comments, accepts it, orders a rerun or dilution, or sends a reactive HIV, hepatitis or drug screen for confirmation.

error.defect_description: Result accepted that needed a rerun.

control.basis: Medical laboratory technologists registered with the College of Medical Laboratory Technologists of Ontario verify results

evidence.note: Common core laboratory practice; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Release the completed profile
steps.description: The technologist checks that every test on the insurer's profile has a result or a not-done comment and that the results sit under the right applicant, then releases the profile in the LIS.

error.defect_description: Profile released with a missing test.

control.basis: Release of results by a registered technologist under the laboratory's licence

evidence.note: Results reviewed and reported within 48 hours (dyn_car). Times are estimates; release is done in batches through the day.

steps.name: Rerun or dilute on the next run
steps.description: The assistant retrieves the aliquot from the rack and reloads it with the dilution or repeat order; the new result returns to the technologist's queue.

evidence.note: Common practice; estimate.

steps.name: Confirm a reactive screen by a second method
steps.description: The technologist repeats the reactive HIV or hepatitis screen in duplicate and sends repeatedly reactive specimens for a confirmatory assay, or sends a positive drug screen for chromatography confirmation, recording each step.

error.defect_description: Confirmation result mismatched to the specimen.

control.basis: Laboratory confirmation algorithm: screening-reactive infectious disease and drug results are confirmed before a positive is reported

evidence.note: Common practice for insurance and clinical screening; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Medical director reviews a confirmed positive
steps.description: The medical director or clinical scientist reviews the confirmed positive HIV or hepatitis result, adds the interpretive comment, and follows the rule for informing the insurer's medical director and, where the applicant consented, the applicant's physician, and any provincial reporting rule.

control.basis: Provincial reportable disease rules and the applicant's signed consent on how positive results are disclosed

evidence.note: Signed notice and consent governs disclosure (dyn_kit2020); express consent for sensitive information (opc_consent). The disclosure path is common practice; reporting rules were not opened, tier B rests on the consent sources.

steps.name: Transmit results to the insurer and the case file
steps.description: The LIS sends the released profile through the insurer exchange in ACORD or the insurer's format to the underwriter and attaches it to the order in the order management system, which marks the lab item complete in iCARE.

next.condition: insurer later asks for an add-on or repeat test

evidence.note: Electronic transmission within 48 hours; ACORD and custom downloads (dyn_car, dyn_adv). Batch interval is an estimate.

steps.name: Report the kit as not testable and ask for a recollection
steps.description: The evidence reviewer records why the kit cannot be tested (no consent, quantity not sufficient, haemolysed, too old, no urine), sends a not-tested result to the case file and tells case management so the insurer can decide on a recollection.

evidence.note: Non-viable specimens may require recollection and the carrier decides (dyn_faq). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Contain a damaged pack
steps.description: The assistant opens a leaking or crushed pack in the biosafety cabinet, salvages intact tubes, disinfects, and records which tubes are lost.

control.basis: Transportation of Dangerous Goods Regulations and laboratory biosafety procedures for Category B specimens

evidence.note: Common practice; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Retrieve the stored specimen for an add-on test
steps.description: Within the retention period an insurer may ask for an add-on or repeat test; the assistant finds the specimen in retention storage by rack position and loads it with the new order.

control.basis: Carrier service terms: specimens kept five weeks for repeat testing

evidence.note: Samples kept five weeks for repeat testing (dyn_car). Request share and timing are estimates.

steps.name: File the specimens in retention storage
steps.description: After the run the assistant files the tubes and aliquots by rack and position in refrigerated storage, where they stay for five weeks in case the insurer asks for repeat testing.

evidence.note: Five-week retention (dyn_car). Times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Missing consent, lab code or label
exceptions.description: The authorization form or seals are incomplete; the kit is held while the evidence reviewer chases the examiner, and about 30 percent cannot be fixed in time.

exceptions.name: Kit does not match an order
exceptions.description: The kit arrives before the electronic order data or with mismatched details and is linked by the evidence reviewer.

exceptions.name: Specimen not testable
exceptions.description: No urine, quantity not sufficient, haemolysed or unspun too long; a not-tested result goes to the case and the insurer decides on recollection.

exceptions.name: Reactive screen confirmation
exceptions.description: A reactive HIV, hepatitis or drug screen is repeated and confirmed; confirmed positives go to the medical director.

exceptions.name: Add-on test within retention
exceptions.description: The insurer asks for an extra or repeat test on the stored specimen within five weeks.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from kit arrival at the laboratory to results transmitted to the insurer
benchmarks.population: Insurance blood and urine kits at a Canadian insurance laboratory

evidence.note: Results generally reported within 48 hours (dyn_car) and three business days on average from collection to delivery (dyn_faq), of which about a day is shipping; the p90 is an estimate for holds and confirmations.

benchmarks.unit: business days on average from collection to results at the carrier

pain_points.description: Paper authorization slips arrive without a signature, lab code or matching labels, and because consent cannot be fixed at the bench the kit waits on the examiner and often ends in a recollection.

evidence.note: Unsigned slips stop testing (crl_instr); incomplete paper entries are a known problem that electronic slips reduce (examone2016).

pain_points.description: Serum left unspun at the examiner's home or delayed in shipping spoils glucose and other analytes and forces recollection.

evidence.note: Centrifuge within 2 to 4 hours (dyn_kit2020); delayed centrifugation errors (examone2016).

pain_points.description: Kits that arrive before the order data or with mistyped details need manual searching in the order system.

evidence.note: Estimate.

pain_points.description: Reactive screen confirmations add one to three days and need medical director time.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: Insurance carriers
sources.supports: Samples are sealed and sent to the laboratory; results generally reported to carriers by electronic transmission within 48 hours or less; samples kept five weeks so repeat tests can be requested; full range of insurance tests and custom profiles; secure online reporting to underwriters and automated downloads in ACORD and custom formats; ePara used by health professionals.

sources.title: Insurance advisors
sources.supports: Results generally reported to carriers within 48 hours or less; laboratories test 40,000 specimens every day; iCARE online order tracking.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions: The model laboratory's insurance testing service order tracker
sources.supports: Average turnaround for blood and urine specimens is three business days from collection until results are delivered to the carrier's underwriting team, for specimens tested in the Canadian laboratories; specimens are couriered to the Brampton laboratory; specimens that become non-viable may need recollection, decided by the carrier.

sources.title: Instructions for blood/urine kit (insurance), version 6
sources.supports: Proposed insured reads and signs the Notice and Consent and Chain of Custody section and signs the tamper-evident seal; examiner completes the laboratory authorization form, labels tubes with the name and pre-printed barcodes and enters the insurer's lab code; urine temperature recorded; urinalysis preservative tube minimum 7 mL; SST clots upright 30 minutes and should be centrifuged within 2 to 4 hours with serum poured into an aliquot tube; kits stored at 2 to 8 C and shipped within one day by Purolator to the Brampton laboratory; specimens are for insurance purposes only, not diagnosis.

sources.title: Insurance collections: specific instructions for examiners
sources.supports: The applicant must read and sign the authorization slip and specimens are not drawn if the applicant declines or alters it; tamper-evident tape carries the applicant's signature and date; urine temperature recorded on the slip; a urine sample is required with all blood profile kits; specimens shipped within 24 hours or the next shipping day and refrigerated until shipped.

sources.title: Hooper Holmes, Inc. annual report on Form 10-K for 2012
sources.supports: Heritage Labs tests blood, urine and oral fluid specimens mainly for life insurance underwriting: profiles detect HIV antibodies, cholesterol and lipids, liver or kidney disorders, hepatitis antibodies, prostate specific antigen, immune disorders, tobacco or nicotine use and certain medications, cocaine and other drugs; about 65 percent of its specimens came from its own paramedical exams; it assembles blood/urine and urine-only kits.

sources.title: Field underwriting guide for life and critical illness insurance
sources.supports: Requirement abbreviations include blood profile and urine HIV; the laboratory uses a high threshold for nicotine detection in the urinalysis, so second-hand smoke does not cause a positive result.

sources.title: Evidence of insurability schedule (form 1343)
sources.publisher: The Equitable Life Insurance Company of Canada
sources.supports: Age and amount grid for paramedical, labs and APS; preferred classes need a paramedical and blood profile with urinalysis; PSA is ordered as part of the blood profile for males; newcomers to Canada need a blood profile with hepatitis screens and urinalysis.

sources.title: Ask the experts: ensuring quality throughout the applicant exam process
sources.supports: Delayed centrifugation causes specimen errors that service-centre exams avoid; about 70 percent of the lab slip is pre-populated from the ordering system and the examiner app flags missing required fields, reducing unreadable or incomplete paper entries.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principle 3: Consent
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Meaningful consent is required; express consent is generally required when the information collected, used or disclosed is sensitive; consent can be withdrawn subject to legal or contractual restrictions.

sources.title: Licences and quality commitment
sources.supports: The Brampton laboratory holds ISO 15189 accreditation, an Ontario licence and CAP accreditation; the quality system includes specimen acceptability protocols, EQA and competency assessment.

sources.title: Wages: Medical technologist, medical laboratory in Ontario (NOC 32120)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 23.00, median 42.00, high 50.00 dollars (2023-2024).

sources.title: Wages: Medical laboratory technical assistant in Ontario (NOC 33101)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 26.25, high 36.00 dollars (2023-2024).

assumptions: Insurance kits come straight to the laboratory by overnight courier (organisation file assumption), so receiving is done by core laboratory assistants rather than community specimen processing.
The analytical run uses the shared core laboratory analysers; instrument time with nobody working is counted as waiting (s11).

About 7 percent of kits have a paperwork or seal deficiency, 8 percent need manual matching to an order, 3 percent are not testable and 25 percent of profiles have at least one held result; these are estimates.

Results go to the insurer and to the case file at the same time; the process map lists only the case review process as the receiver, so the direct delivery to the insurer is described in s18 but not listed as an interface.
Some carriers send their kits to US laboratories they prefer; those kits are outside this workflow (dyn_faq describes this routing in recent years).
Disclosure of confirmed positive HIV and hepatitis results follows the applicant's consent and provincial rules; the exact rules were not opened, so s17 is described as common practice.
